layers.name: Terrain height
layers.source: NRCan HRDEM lidar DTM and DSM, project QC-600023_52_CMM_2023, 1 m, averaged to 2 m

layers.name: Canopy height
layers.source: NRCan HRDEM lidar DTM and DSM, project QC-600023_52_CMM_2023, 1 m, averaged to 2 m

layers.name: Hillshade
layers.source: NRCan HRDEM lidar DTM and DSM, project QC-600023_52_CMM_2023, 1 m, averaged to 2 m
layers.note: sun from the north-west at 45 degrees

layers.name: Slope
layers.source: NRCan HRDEM lidar DTM and DSM, project QC-600023_52_CMM_2023, 1 m, averaged to 2 m

layers.name: Wetness index
layers.source: NRCan HRDEM lidar DTM and DSM, project QC-600023_52_CMM_2023, 1 m, averaged to 2 m
layers.note: ln(a / tan b), Beven and Kirkby 1979; multiple flow directions (Freeman 1991) on the 3 x 3 smoothed lidar DTM; flow from outside the parcel is not counted

layers.name: Vegetation (NDVI)
layers.source: NASA HLS v2 (NASA/USGS Landsat 8/9 L30 and ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 S30), 30 m
layers.note: mean of 24 clear June to August scenes

layers.name: Spring surface temperature
layers.source: USGS Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature (band 10), 100 m thermal, distributed at 30 m
layers.note: mean anomaly of 32 clear April and May scenes

layers.name: Soil map unit

components.name: Saint-Laurent
components.texture: mineral, surface layer 0-29 cm: 37 % clay, 2.7 % organic carbon
components.source: AAFC CanSIS soil name and layer tables, Quebec v2r20130705, SIE

components.name: Sainte-Rosalie
components.texture: mineral, surface layer 0-15 cm: 56 % clay, 2.6 % organic carbon
components.source: AAFC CanSIS soil name and layer tables, Quebec v2r20130705, SSL

layers.source: IRDA, Cartes pédologiques du Québec, sheets 31H12-101 to 202 (study 41, 1:20 000); AAFC CanSIS soil name and layer tables, Quebec v2r20130705; Lajoie and Baril, Les sols des îles de Montréal, Jésus et Bizard (CanSIS soil survey report PQ41)

layers.name: Scouting zones
layers.source: k-means classes of wetness index (30 m mean), NDVI, spring surface temperature and soil map unit
layers.note: classes for spreading traps; not a risk prediction

layers.name: Crop 2025
layers.source: AAFC Annual Crop Inventory, 30 m (Open Government Licence - Canada)

pocket.rule: lowest 15 % of parcel cells by lidar height

open.rule: under 2 m of canopy, at least 60% such cells in the 30 m around, summer NDVI of 0.35 or more, on a mapped soil unit, inside the field outline, 15 m from the edge of the square (Taupin choices)

crops.source: AAFC Annual Crop Inventory, 30 m (Open Government Licence - Canada), 2011 to 2025; crop = most common class over the open cells

trap_rules.source: RAP Grandes cultures, Méthode standard de dépistage des vers fil-de-fer (Agri-Réseau doc. 115269, 16 April 2025)

sources.terrain: NRCan HRDEM lidar DTM and DSM, project QC-600023_52_CMM_2023, 1 m, averaged to 2 m; hillshade, slope and wetness index computed from the DTM
sources.trees: canopy height = lidar DSM minus DTM; a crown is drawn at each 14 m local maximum above 3 m, inside the outline
sources.ndvi: NASA HLS v2 (NASA/USGS Landsat 8/9 L30 and ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 S30), 30 m, 2020-06-20 to 2025-08-12
sources.lst: USGS Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature (band 10), 100 m thermal, distributed at 30 m, 2016-04-29 to 2025-05-01
sources.soil: IRDA, Cartes pédologiques du Québec, sheets 31H12-101 to 202 (study 41, 1:20 000); AAFC CanSIS soil name and layer tables, Quebec v2r20130705; Lajoie and Baril, Les sols des îles de Montréal, Jésus et Bizard (CanSIS soil survey report PQ41)
sources.pocket: lowest 15 % of parcel cells by lidar height
sources.traps: RAP Grandes cultures, Méthode standard de dépistage des vers fil-de-fer (Agri-Réseau doc. 115269, 16 April 2025)
